title: 24 April 1990. Hubble launched with a mirror that was the wrong shape.
description:
Hubble launched with a mirror that was the wrong shape. Within weeks, its first images came back blurred.

How much too flat the edge of the 2.4 metre mirror was. NASA puts it at about one fiftieth the thickness of a human hair.

A test instrument had been put together wrongly. The Allen Commission found the null corrector was incorrectly assembled, with one lens 1.3 millimetres out of position.

Astronauts fitted it with glasses. COSTAR, the size of a telephone booth, carried five pairs of corrective mirrors in front of three instruments.

The repair flew on Space Shuttle Endeavour. Mission STS-61 ran from 2 to 13 December 1993.

A flaw thinner than a hair needed a shuttle to fix.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubble_Space_Telescope: read. Established that the primary mirror was 2.4 m across; launch on 24 April 1990 aboard Space Shuttle Discovery (STS-31); that images within weeks showed the problem; that the outer edge was too flat by about 2200 nanometres (2.2 micrometres); that the Allen Commission found a reflective null corrector had been incorrectly assembled with one lens out of position by 1.3 mm; and that COSTAR was installed in 1993 on the first servicing mission, STS-61, in December 1993.
- https://asd.gsfc.nasa.gov/archive/hubble/missions/sm1.html: read (NASA Goddard archive). Established that the edge was ground too flat by 2.2 microns, roughly one fiftieth the thickness of a human hair; that this caused spherical aberration and fuzzy images; that COSTAR was a telephone booth sized instrument with five pairs of corrective mirrors placed in front of the Faint Object Camera, Faint Object Spectrograph and Goddard High Resolution Spectrograph; and that STS-61 aboard Endeavour flew from 2 to 13 December 1993.
